sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents and perused the record.
3.

The case of the petitioner is that based on two crimes viz., Crime No.130/2022 of Bhongiri Rural Police Station registered for the offences under Sections 457, 380 and 411 I.P.C., and Crime No.135/2022 of Valigonda Police Station registered for the offences under Sections 356 and 379 I.P.C, the respondent No.2 has passed the impugned detention order dated 11.08.2022.
The detenue is Accused No.3 in Crime No.130/2022 and Accused No.2 in Crime No.135 of 2022.

It is further stated that the detention orders passed against the Accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No.130/2022 were already set aside by this Court vide orders passed in W.P.No.32045 of 2022 and W.P.No.34487 of 2022, dated 12.09.2022 and 26.10.2022 respectively, and ultimately, prayed to set aside the impugned detention order and the consequential confirmation order.
AAR,J & JS,J 4.
The learned Special Government Pleader does not dispute the above submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

sentences.text: As seen from the material placed on record and the submissions made, it is clear that the detention orders passed against Accused Nos.1 and 2 in Crime No.130/2022 were already set aside by this Court vide orders passed in W.P.No.32045 of 2022 and W.P.No.34487 of 2022, dated 12.09.2022 and 26.10.2022 respectively.

Moreover, the impugned detention order was passed without adhering to the requirements/mandate given under Section 3(2) of the PD Act and by relying only on two crimes registered for the offences punishable under Sections 356, 379, 380, 457 and 411 I.P.C., which do not add up to "disturbing the public order" and which is only a "law and order"
problem.

Under these circumstances and since the facts and circumstances of the present case are akin to the facts and circumstances in W.P.No.32045 of 2022 and W.P.No.34487 of 2022, dated 12.09.2022 and 26.10.2022 respectively, the impugned orders are liable to be set aside.
6. In the result, the Writ Petition is allowed.

The impugned detention order vide No.122/PD-CELL/CCRB/RCKD/2022, dated 11.08.2022, passed by the respondent No.2, and the consequential AAR,J & JS,J confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.1948, dated 17.10.2022, are hereby set aside.
The respondents are directed to set the detenu, namely, Angadi Jampaiah S/o. Venkataiah at liberty forthwith, in case he is no longer required in any other criminal case.
Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
